title: feat(2d): rest Adaptive planned on proved remaining stock
body:
## What changed

A new generator in the motion crate: `camcraft_motion::machining2d::rest_adaptive(region, params, stock)` - 2D rest machining with the Adaptive strategy, planned on the remaining stock the earlier operations are **proved** to have left. Nothing is assumed cut: no entry bore, no full pocket, no entered previous diameter.

Not stacked. It needs none of #1817's code and merges cleanly with it (checked with `git merge-tree` against `issue/1489-rest-pocket-param` and against main). The Pocket operation's door (`rest2d::rest_strategy`) is untouched and **still refuses Adaptive for rest machining**: the operation only has an entered previous tool, which is no proof. Lifting that refusal belongs to #2033, which produces the `RestStock` this generator reads (the contract is written on #2033).

New code, all under `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/`:

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `rest/stock.rs` | `RestStock`, `StockFloor`: proved floors; the stock and depth guards |
| `rest/entry.rs` | where a plunge is proved clear; the entry guard |
| `rest/peel.rs` | one cut depth: areas, phases, the step ladder, budget, coverage |
| `rest/runs.rs` | the cutting runs: the boundary of the opened room, where it bites |
| `rest/pass.rs` | one pass on trial: legal, crossing-free, walked on the raster, kept or not |
| `rest/leads.rs` | how a pass is reached: stay-down link, or retract and a proved plunge |
| `rest/canon.rs` | the walls as one fixed vertex list (what keeps passes from crossing) |
| `rest/post.rs` | the moves |
| `raster/conservative.rs` | the stock raster read large; proof-of-air and cut queries |

### The contract (the issue's design decision)

- **Separate regions per cut depth**: the legal cutter-center area (pocket less tool radius and stock to leave) and a conservative bound on the material standing at that depth.
- **Stock**: a `StockFloor { z, remaining, uncertain }` claims that inside the pocket, at and above `z`, material stands only in `remaining` or `uncertain`. There is no constructor from a tool diameter.
- **Three guards**, each pinned by a test that runs the planner with that guard off and shows the pin fail:
  - stock - `uncertain` stands as material;
  - depth - a cut depth below every proved floor is refused by name, before anything is planned;
  - entry - a plunge needs the whole footprint plus a margin (0.1 mm or four cells) proved clear by the stock as given, asked of the polygon and of the raster. What this operation's own passes cleared is never credited to a plunge.
- **Conservative raster**: every cell the bound touches stands (the bound is grown by a cell's half diagonal before sampling).
- **Load**: every feed, lead and link included, is walked on that raster before it is kept. No overload fallback.
- **Refused by name**: no proved floor; a cut depth below every proved floor; no entry with proved clearance; a load that cannot be held (with the place); coverage that cannot be proved; a plan past its budget; nothing left to cut.

### The plan

The room is the legal center area minus the material grown by (tool radius - step). It is opened by a disc whose radius falls phase by phase; a pass is the room's boundary where it bites. That gives arcs tangent to both walls in a corner, half loops across a neck, and closed rings round a piece that touches no wall. Passes that ride a wall ride it on one fixed vertex list and retrace the area's earlier way in and out, so the verifier's exact-sign crossing law holds; each candidate is still asked that law. Details, what was tried and dropped, and readings: `docs/decisions/2031-rest-adaptive.md`.

Literature (cited in each module's provenance): Held, LNCS 500 (1991); Yao, Gupta and Nau, CAD 35(9) (2003); Stori and Wright, J. Manuf. Systems 19(3) (2000); Serra, Image Analysis and Mathematical Morphology (1982); Otkur and Lazoglu, IJMTM 47 (2007); Altintas, Manufacturing Automation (2012); Hasselgren et al., GPU Gems 2 (2005). No other CAM product's code or output was consulted.

## Readings

4 mm tool after a 12 mm Waterline roughing pass, depths Z-2 and Z-4, optimal load 14.6% of D. "Measured" is `quality::measure` on an independent column stock that the roughing path was cut into.

| Fixture | Passes a depth | Plunges a depth | Worst planned load | Measured | Cut / air feed / rapid (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 x 40, 3 mm corners | 40 | 4 | 14.4% | 13.1% | 224 / 967 / 360 |
| 70 x 50 with a 14 x 14 island | 36 | 4 | 13.4% | 13.5% | 250 / 955 / 450 |
| two bays, 10 mm neck | 128 | 37 | 15.4% | 15.1% | 954 / 3445 / 1337 |

## How tested

`crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/` (new suite, 9 tests, 36 s wall in debug). `sim.rs` simulates the roughing pass on a column stock, derives the proved stock from it, checks that bound against the simulation, and holds every rest path to: verifier clean; no rapid below the top of the stock except straight up; every plunge down a column the **earlier** operation cleared for the whole footprint; no descent bites; no slotting; the load at each requested depth within 5% of optimal; rest left in reach under 0.05 mm2.

- `four_corner_residues_are_cut_from_proved_stock_within_the_load`
- `a_conventional_cut_leaving_stock_on_the_walls_keeps_every_law`
- `an_island_and_disconnected_rest_areas_are_each_entered_from_proved_space`
- `a_neck_the_earlier_tool_could_not_pass_is_cut_through_within_the_load`
- `a_neck_too_narrow_to_hold_the_load_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_pocket_corner_too_sharp_to_turn_in_within_the_load_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_roughing_pass_that_stops_above_the_rest_floor_is_refused_by_name`
- `stock_that_is_not_proved_is_refused_by_name`
- `degenerate_input_errors_and_never_panics`

Unit tests, `adaptive/rest/tests.rs` (the guard mutations):

- `without_the_stock_guard_a_plunge_lands_in_uncertain_stock`
- `without_the_depth_guard_a_plunge_goes_below_the_proved_floor`
- `without_the_entry_guard_a_plunge_lands_on_material`
- `the_conservative_raster_stands_every_cell_a_sliver_touches`
- `a_wall_stretch_is_walked_on_the_walls_own_vertices`
- `the_phase_radii_fall_gently_and_end_sharp`

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 9916b459d (the code commit): motion suites ok in 418 s (51 binaries and the lib tests), app suites ok in 212 s (47 binaries), 0 failed, wall 10.6 min. The head adds one docs-only commit (`docs/decisions/2031-rest-adaptive.md`) after it. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. The three tests the gate names as slow (>60 s) are existing `adaptive_troch` unit tests, not this PR's.

## Known limits, and what was not exercised

- **Sharp pocket corners are refused** (a center arc of 1.0 mm is cut by a 4 mm tool, 0.7 mm is refused, a square corner always is), and so is a **neck under about 2.5 tool diameters**. Both are named refusals with the place, pinned by tests. Follow-up #2108 asks the maintainer what they should get instead.
- **Air feed is about four times the cut length**, and a neck takes 37 plunges a depth. The plain Adaptive's 1.5x budget is not applied. Follow-up #2109.
- **The measured load depends on the measuring grid.** The table and the tests measure on the planner's grid (D/120, the heavy lane's). On the default D/80 grid the same paths read up to 17.4% of D in a concave corner: the yardstick reads on a rim a cell and a half outside the cutter, which stands in more wall on a coarser grid.
- The posted path is chords only (no arc fit): 3216 moves for the corner fixture.
- Not exercised: a stock with more than one distinct floor region (the fixtures' floors are equal at both depths); a stock built from a grid (staircase outlines); `with_film` values other than the default; inch-scale or very large pockets (planning time 3.6 to 19 s per distinct depth here, debug build); the centre-cutting plunge law of the app pipeline (the generator is not wired to an operation, so nothing posts from it yet).
- `adaptive/raster.rs` grows by one line (`mod conservative;`) to 404 lines; it was 403.
- No MCP tool: no user-facing command is added.

Process change: no.

Changelog: 2D rest machining: an Adaptive generator planned on the proved remaining stock of earlier operations (`rest_adaptive`, motion crate); not reachable from the Pocket operation until the stock is derived (#2033)

Effort: max (not escalated).

Fixes #2031
